newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: Common market vital for southern Africa - Mandela.
newsitem.headline: Common market vital for southern Africa - Mandela.

text.p: Southern Africa has no choice but to develop a regional common market if it wants to compete on the global stage, South Africa's President Nelson Mandela said on Wednesday.
"No country in southern Africa can succeed on its own," he told a World Economic Forum (WEF) conference in the Zimbabwean capital Harare.
"Inter-dependence amongst neig(bours and the pressures of a globalised economy increasingly defined by regional blocks dictate that we work togeher as a region."
The 12-nation Southern African Development Community (SADC) plans to create a free trade area within eight years, a task Mandela acknowledged would not be easy.
"We have set out on the path to a single regional market, in the knowledge that it is no easy path," he said.
Barriers to trade within the region had to be dismantled in a way which took account of the relative strength of the different economies, he said.
"We cannot reduce tariffs only for the benefits to accrue to the stronger partner," he said.
"Integration that causes destructive movement of capital, skills or labour defeats our purposes."
SADC consists of Angola, Botswana, Malawi, Mozambique, Mauritius, Lesotho, Namibia, Tanzania, South Africa, Swaziland, Zambia and Zimbabwe.
South Africa's Foreign Minister Alfred Nzo said earlier on Wednesday that Laurent Kabila's former Zaire could join the grouping at a later date.
